source.snippet: I am currently in need of a software that sits between my web browser and the internet and acts like a HTTP(S) proxy, but which can manipulate the pages that the browser sees on-the-fly. For example, I would like to be able to change certain attributes of HTML elements before the page is delivered to the browser. I am aware of extensions like TamperMonkey and GreaseMonkey, and I have used them successfully sometimes. But in this case, they are obviously not appropriate for the task.

problem_statement: Developers and QA engineers need a local HTTPS-intercepting proxy that can modify response HTML/DOM on-the-fly before delivery to the browser, but existing browser extension solutions (TamperMonkey, GreaseMonkey) are insufficient for cases where extension-layer access is unavailable or the modification must be transparent to the page itself.
target_segment: Web developers, QA engineers, and web archivists who need transparent browser-level HTTP interception with DOM rewriting capabilities
notes: Poster is a technical user with a specific professional workflow need (web archiving/DOM attribute manipulation) that existing free tools don't solve. This is a tooling purchase context — developers and QA teams regularly pay for proxy tools (Charles Proxy ~$50, Proxyman ~$100, Burp Suite Professional $449/yr). The gap is a no-code or low-code GUI tool for DOM rewriting rules layered on top of MITM proxy infrastructure. Single signal here but the Charles/Proxyman market validates willingness to pay in this segment.
